answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds agent identities to a cryptographic stake burning curve where verification costs scale quadratically, O(k^2), creating superlinear economic friction. Every agent must stake and burn tokens within a hierarchical terrace structure: activating an initial node is cheap, but each concurrent clone in this oasis requires escalating sacrifices. A validator uses a lotus commitment scheme to enforce irreversible proof of burn, ensuring exponential attacker cost that renders mass identity generation mathematically unprofitable.
